operating_mode.input: You take in material that is not yet packaged: primary sources, raw cases, a problem nobody has framed. The heaviest force in your chart is Indirect Resource, appearing on the month stem and repeating in the hidden stems of the month, day, and hour branches. That means your intake is self-directed — you open the file, test small cases, and keep notes nobody asked for. You do not wait for a syllabus. You go deeper than the room because the research center is the strongest single weight in the chart, and the balanced Day Master means this intake feeds you rather than draining you.
operating_mode.processing: You convert what you learn into a small, repeatable service — a template, a checklist, a short engagement. Direct Wealth is tied with Rob Wealth as the second-heaviest force, showing on the year stem and in hidden stems of the year and day branches. So the middle of your loop is not a big launch but a modest, reliable conversion. You price it modestly, deliver it, and improve the same offer rather than inventing a new one. The processing step is incremental by structure, not by preference.
operating_mode.output: Your output is a working model in your head that you can apply the next time the same problem appears, plus a small delivered service that peers notice. Rob Wealth sits on the hour stem and ties with Direct Wealth, so the output step triggers competition: someone starts offering what you built. You then go back to the source, add a layer they have not copied, and make your version harder to replace. The output is rarely a finished public artifact — it is a defended position that keeps moving.
operating_mode.recovery: You recharge by returning to private study. The loop runs from Indirect Resource into peer competition, and when defense drains you, the structure sends you back to the research center to recover. That is why the ten years starting around age 48, the Gui Wei pillar, matters: the pull toward private study loosens there, and it becomes easier to let work leave your desk. Until then, recovery means going deeper alone, not resting in a group.

failure_environments.env: A setting where formal standing gates everything: long approval chains, title-based permission, a culture where work does not move until a role signs off.
failure_environments.mechanism: Direct Officer carries no weight in your chart — no stem or hidden stem classifies under it. So waiting for formal standing stalls the income step that closes your loop. Research piles up on the desk, the incremental conversions do not accumulate, and the visible result is slow. The failure is not that you lack talent; it is that the environment asks you to wait for something your structure does not supply, and the handover date slips while you look for permission.

failure_environments.env: A room where peer contest is constant and loud, with no private-study center to return to.
failure_environments.mechanism: Rob Wealth sits on the hour stem and ties with Direct Wealth as the second-heaviest force, so defense is a structural step in your loop. But when competition is the whole room, defense drains the private-study center that feeds you. You go back to research to recover instead of forward to conversion. The loop runs in low gear: the file stays almost ready for weeks, and the meeting correction replaces a shipped offer. The environment turns a healthy defense step into a permanent pause.

failure_environments.env: A large team where your private study is treated as overhead rather than billable work, and client contact is filtered through account managers.
failure_environments.mechanism: Your loop needs a short path from finding to buyer. Direct Wealth shows on the year stem and in hidden stems of the year and day branches, and the balanced Day Master means the wealth step is not a stretch — it is the natural middle of the loop. When that path is long, the conversion step never completes, and the research center keeps feeding a loop that cannot close. You keep reinvesting in depth, but visible results accumulate slowly and you rarely get to point at something finished.

ideal_life_structure.time: You need long, protected blocks for private research and a fixed handover date on each piece of work. The heaviest force is Indirect Resource, so your time structure should let you go deep alone without interruption, then force a delivery. Set a date and hand over even if it feels unfinished — that is the fix for the leak in your loop. A calendar with open mornings and a hard deadline for each conversion suits you better than a day broken into meetings.
ideal_life_structure.collaboration: Small teams and direct client contact suit you. A manager who asks for a handover date rather than a permission slip is the right counterpart. Collaboration density should be low enough that peer competition is present but not the whole room — you can defend ground without it becoming your job. Metal and earth are named as favorable elements, and the balanced Day Master means research energy feeds the core, so a setting where your private study is treated as billable work lets the loop complete.
ideal_life_structure.feedback_cycle: Short, concrete feedback cycles work best: you deliver a small service, a client uses it, you improve the same offer. Direct Wealth is tied with Rob Wealth as the second-heaviest force, so the income step is incremental and repeatable. You keep a mental ledger of which findings actually paid and which only interested you. Feedback should come from the buyer, not from a title-holder, because formal position carries no weight in your chart.
ideal_life_structure.income_rhythm: Steady, incremental income built bit by bit suits your structure. You do not chase a single large payout. You take what you have learned and turn it into a small, repeatable service, price it modestly, deliver it reliably, and improve the same offer. Over a year the sum is visible, but at any single moment it looks unremarkable. The ten years starting around age 48, the Gui Wei pillar, loosen the pull toward private study and make it easier to let work leave your desk and reach other people.

stability_vs_volatility.verdict: You are better suited to a stable structure with controlled variance, not a high-variance life.
stability_vs_volatility.reason: Your loop runs from private research into steady, incremental income, then into peer defense, then back to research. Direct Wealth and Rob Wealth are tied as the second-heaviest forces, so the income step is incremental by structure, not by preference. A high-variance path would skip the middle conversion step and send you straight from research into competition, which drains the private-study center that feeds you. The balanced Day Master and the favorable elements metal and earth mean the research energy feeds the core rather than draining it — but only when the loop completes.
stability_vs_volatility.precondition: The precondition is a short path from finding to buyer and a handover date you set yourself. If you have direct client contact, a manager who asks for a delivery date rather than a permission slip, and room to go deep alone, you can carry more variance inside a stable frame. Without those, variance turns into a permanent pause: the file stays almost ready, and the defense step replaces the shipped offer.

environment_checklist: Will I have direct contact with the person who uses my work, or will my findings pass through a chain of account managers and approvers? If the path from finding to buyer is long, my conversion step never completes.
Does this setting ask for a handover date, or does it ask for a permission slip? Formal position carries no weight in my chart, so a title-based gate stalls the income step that closes my loop.

Is there room to go deep alone for long blocks, or is my calendar broken into meetings? The heaviest force in my chart is private research, and I recharge by returning to it, not by resting in a group.

Is peer competition present but not the whole room? Rob Wealth ties with Direct Wealth as the second-heaviest force, so defense is a structural step — but when competition is constant and loud, it drains the private-study center that feeds me.

Will my private study be treated as billable work or as overhead? Metal and earth are my favorable elements, and the balanced Day Master means research feeds my core — but only if the environment lets that research reach a buyer.
